App details

Ott e!

A touch game for cats, with moving prey and play settings you can adjust.

Coming soonIn developmentAndroid

What it’s for

A moving prey appears one at a time for the cat to chase and tap. Each species moves differently and reacts to successful touches. Choose playtime and prey before starting; settings stay hidden while the cat plays.

Main features

  • Fly, mosquito, ladybird, beetle, cockroach, grasshopper and spider.
  • Choose 1, 3, 5, 10, 15 or 20 minutes, plus prey, sound and vibration.
  • Full-screen play on tablets and phones.
  • Offline, ad-free play without an account.

The app is being tested. See Availability below for its current download status.

Features in detail

Play and owner controls

Starting a game for your cat

Set the duration and allowed creatures in owner mode, then start. A single creature moves across a clean full-screen play area. Your cat taps it to catch it; no scores or account are needed. Phones and tablets support portrait and landscape, with more space on a larger screen.

Fly, mosquito and ladybug

The fly has fast, unpredictable flight; the mosquito is tiny and fast; the ladybug crawls more slowly and takes short flights. Each is caught with one successful touch. Choose which creatures may appear; at least one of the seven must stay enabled.

Beetle, cockroach, grasshopper and spider

The beetle is more resistant, the cockroach runs quickly along the ground, the grasshopper jumps and changes direction, and the spider crawls. They need two successful touches. After the first touch the creature pauses while held, then escapes after release; the same creature can return from the edge.

Touches and misses

A touch on the visible creature counts as one hit, with a short vibration if enabled. A close miss can make it escape without reducing the hits it still needs; distant touches have no effect. When caught it disappears, followed by a short rest before the next creature.

Sound, visual attention and vibration

Creatures can arrive sound-first, picture-first, together, or picture-only. Short local sounds attract attention; there is no continuous loop. Turn sound and hit vibration on or off separately. Every event still shows the creature when sound is off; unsupported vibration does not stop play.

Game duration and ending

Choose 1, 3, 5, 10, 15 or 20 minutes; the default is 10. Only active play time counts. At the end, creatures and sounds stop and a time-expired message remains on the play area. Return to owner mode and start explicitly for a new game.

Owner mode and continuation

Drag the top-left key to the top-right house/lock to pause and open owner mode. A short demonstration appears at each start. Continue resumes the same creature and remaining time. Home, a new game, or changing duration or allowed creatures discards the old game; settings alone do not start another.

Interruptions and saved settings

App switching, screen-off or a phone interruption pauses movement, sound and the play timer. Return and choose Continue when a game remains. Restarting the app keeps your settings, not the active game. Choose one of eight languages; device brightness stays under your control.

A hidden About surprise

Tap the About logo seven times for an offline scene: a golden creature is caught by a cat paw, followed by Sztella’s photo. Close the photo to return. Six golden species cycle in order; this scene does not appear during the cat’s normal game.

Offline and ad-free

The game, pictures and sounds are local. No account, ads or in-app purchases are needed. The game does not request camera, microphone, location or contacts. Voluntary support opens the JN86 website and gives no game advantage; that external visit may use internet.

Availability

Coming soon. The game is implemented and being prepared for public availability; a closed test is not a public release.
